figures.alt: Photo of a house in a snowy Michigan neighborhood at dusk with warm light glowing in the windows.
figures.caption: Electricity makes lights glow, but only when the circuit is a complete loop.

figures.alt: Two circuits made of a battery, a bulb and wire. Top: the loop has a gap on the right, so the bulb is off. Bottom: the loop is complete, orange arrows show charges moving around the whole loop together, and the bulb glows with rays around it.
figures.caption: The bulb lights only when the loop is closed all the way around. A gap anywhere stops the current in the whole loop.

figures.alt: Table drawn with dots. Bulb lit with paper clip: yes. Foil: yes. String: no. Plastic: no. Wood: no. Switch closed: yes. Switch open: no.
figures.caption: Material tester: paper clip and foil let the bulb light. String, plastic and wood did not. The switch closed lit the bulb and open did not.
